title: Completing the Square for Circle Equations

practice.prompt: Complete the square and write the circle equation in center-radius form: x² + y² − 4x − 6y − 3 = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 4 to complete the x-square and 9 to complete the y-square. This gives (x−2)² + (y−3)² = 16. The center is (2, 3) and radius squared is 16.

practice.prompt: Find the center and radius, then give standard form: x² + y² + 2x − 8y + 8 = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 1 to complete the x-square and 16 to complete the y-square. This gives (x+1)² + (y−4)² = 9. The center is (-1, 4) and radius squared is 9.

practice.prompt: Rewrite the general equation by completing both squares: x² + y² + 4y − 21 = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 0 to complete the x-square and 4 to complete the y-square. This gives x² + (y+2)² = 25. The center is (0, -2) and radius squared is 25.

practice.prompt: Show the completed-square equation and identify its radius: x² + y² + 6x + 4y − 23 = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 9 to complete the x-square and 4 to complete the y-square. This gives (x+3)² + (y+2)² = 36. The center is (-3, -2) and radius squared is 36.

practice.prompt: Which standard-form equation represents this circle? x² + y² − 8x + 9 = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 16 to complete the x-square and 0 to complete the y-square. This gives (x−4)² + y² = 7. The center is (4, 0) and radius squared is 7.

practice.prompt: Determine the center and squared radius from: x² + y² − 2x + 10y + 13 = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 1 to complete the x-square and 25 to complete the y-square. This gives (x−1)² + (y+5)² = 13. The center is (1, -5) and radius squared is 13.

practice.prompt: Complete both squares and state the equation: x² + y² + 4x − 12y − 9 = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 4 to complete the x-square and 36 to complete the y-square. This gives (x+2)² + (y−6)² = 49. The center is (-2, 6) and radius squared is 49.

practice.prompt: Rewrite the equation and explain whether the circle passes through the origin: x² + y² − 6x + 8y = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 9 to complete the x-square and 16 to complete the y-square. This gives (x−3)² + (y+4)² = 25. The center is (3, -4) and radius squared is 25.

practice.prompt: Find the center and exact radius from: x² + y² + 10x − 2y + 16 = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 25 to complete the x-square and 1 to complete the y-square. This gives (x+5)² + (y−1)² = 10. The center is (-5, 1) and radius squared is 10.

practice.prompt: Rewrite this equation; do not confuse r with r²: x² + y² − 12x + 4y + 24 = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 36 to complete the x-square and 4 to complete the y-square. This gives (x−6)² + (y+2)² = 16. The center is (6, -2) and radius squared is 16.

practice.prompt: Identify the center and squared radius after completing the square: x² + y² + 8x + 6y + 20 = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 16 to complete the x-square and 9 to complete the y-square. This gives (x+4)² + (y+3)² = 5. The center is (-4, -3) and radius squared is 5.

practice.prompt: Give the standard form and radius from: x² + y² − 4x + 14y − 11 = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 4 to complete the x-square and 49 to complete the y-square. This gives (x−2)² + (y+7)² = 64. The center is (2, -7) and radius squared is 64.

practice.prompt: Find the center and check the sign inside each square: x² + y² + 2x + 12y + 29 = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 1 to complete the x-square and 36 to complete the y-square. This gives (x+1)² + (y+6)² = 8. The center is (-1, -6) and radius squared is 8.

practice.prompt: Complete squares when the constant on the right is zero: x² + y² − 10x − 10y = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 25 to complete the x-square and 25 to complete the y-square. This gives (x−5)² + (y−5)² = 50. The center is (5, 5) and radius squared is 50.

practice.prompt: Find the radius squared and center from: x² + y² + 14x − 4y − 12 = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 49 to complete the x-square and 4 to complete the y-square. This gives (x+7)² + (y−2)² = 65. The center is (-7, 2) and radius squared is 65.

practice.prompt: Rewrite the circle equation and check the origin: x² + y² − 2x − 2y = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 1 to complete the x-square and 1 to complete the y-square. This gives (x−1)² + (y−1)² = 2. The center is (1, 1) and radius squared is 2.

practice.prompt: Challenge: complete the squares even though the center has half-integer coordinates: x² + y² − x + 3y − 4 = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 0.25 to complete the x-square and 2.25 to complete the y-square. This gives (x−1/2)² + (y+3/2)² = 13/2. The center is (1/2, −3/2) and radius squared is 13/2.

practice.prompt: Challenge: recover the center and exact radius squared from odd linear coefficients: x² + y² + 3x − 5y − 3 = 0
practice.steps: Group x and y terms. Add 2.25 to complete the x-square and 6.25 to complete the y-square. This gives (x+3/2)² + (y−5/2)² = 23/2. The center is (−3/2, 5/2) and radius squared is 23/2.

test.steps: Half the x coefficient to get −h and the y coefficient to get −k; complete both squares to obtain (x−1)² + (y−2)² = 9.
Half the x coefficient to get −h and the y coefficient to get −k; complete both squares to obtain (x+3)² + y² = 4.
Half the x coefficient to get −h and the y coefficient to get −k; complete both squares to obtain (x−2)² + (y+3)² = 5.
Half the x coefficient to get −h and the y coefficient to get −k; complete both squares to obtain (x+2)² + (y−4)² = 20.

test.prompt: Complete the square: x² + y² − x + 5y − 3 = 0
test.steps: Half the x coefficient to get −h and the y coefficient to get −k; complete both squares to obtain (x−1/2)² + (y+5/2)² = 19/2.

english: A circle equation can be rewritten by completing squares in x and y.
Group the x terms, group the y terms, and move the constant to the right.
For x² + Dx, add (D/2)² to form (x+D/2)². Do the same for y.
Add the same quantities to both sides. The right-hand side becomes r².
The center is the opposite of the signs inside the squared brackets: (2,3). The radius is 4.
Odd linear coefficients give half-integer center coordinates. Fractions are valid.
Check by expanding your completed squares and recovering the original equation.
arabic: يمكن إعادة كتابة معادلة الدائرة بإكمال المربع في س وص.
اجمع حدود س وحدود ص، وانقل الحد الثابت إلى الطرف الآخر.
لإكمال مربع س، أضف مربع نصف معامل س. كرر الخطوة مع ص.
أضف المقدارين نفسيهما إلى طرفي المعادلة، لتحصل على مربع نصف القطر.
مثال: س تربيع زائد ص تربيع ناقص أربعة س ناقص ستة ص ناقص ثلاثة يساوي صفر؛ المركز اثنان وثلاثة ومربع نصف القطر ستة عشر.
إشارة المركز عكس الإشارة داخل القوسين، ونصف القطر هو الجذر التربيعي للطرف الأيمن.
إذا كان المعامل فرديا فقد تظهر إحداثيات كسرية للمركز، وهذا صحيح.
تحقق من الحل بفك المربعات واستعادة المعادلة الأصلية.
